reviewer: GPT-6 Astra model review; not human approval

authority.locator: Public Health Law 2807-k(9), revision displayed 2026-05-29; accessed 2026-11-08
authority.quote: utilizing only a uniform financial assistance form developed and provided by the department
authority.interpretation: The statute requires the department's uniform form. This passage does not define permissible logo/MRN/row/layout changes or CSS's scoring overlap. The official reference itself supplies hospital-name and telephone placeholders. No verified customization ruling or approved CSS whole-form scoring rule was obtained in this review.

resolved_points: Hospital contact substitution is contemplated by the official HOSPITAL NAME and PHONE NUMBER placeholders (reference-38); it is not a missing section.

All 80 extracted reference units are accounted for by normalized text correspondence or explicitly reviewed differences. This coverage check supplements, rather than substitutes for, the visual review.

The six-person official 300% cell is visibly $133,880. HHS arithmetic is $44,360 x 3 = $133,080. Little Falls's correction is not a dollar-check failure. Whether a literal-copy whole-form rule permits that correction remains a rubric question, not an arithmetic uncertainty.

Both hospitals retain patient identity, household information, insurance questions, medical-expense amount, responsible-party certification/signature/date, rights, eligibility, discounts, installments and all nine income-proof categories. No missing section was identified in the reviewed renders.
limitations: Local Word rendering, not a hospital-published PDF for the DOCX sources. Pagination can vary with fonts, printer settings and Word versions. Every page was visually inspected in this session; this is model review, not human or NYS approval. The original snapshots are preserved.

362.conclusion: Content and visual completeness are supported: all required sections and writable fields were found across five rendered pages. The remaining whole-form uncertainty is the permitted-customization rule for campus/MRN additions, the eighth household row and the HHS-corrected official typo. It is no longer an extraction or unrendered-layout blocker.
362.recommendation: Under a content-preserving customization rule, recommend yes for entire-form completeness. That rule has not been approved; retain unclear rather than infer a legal authorization or human decision.
questions: CSS rubric owner, or NYS DOH for legal form requirements: may campus/MRN additions, the eighth household row and corrected HHS arithmetic count as use of the entire Uniform Application when all required content is retained? Approve a cited rule before resolving this draft.
